Senaki Jewish Cemetery (Jewish section in Menji Municipal Cemetery)

Jewish Cemetery · Senaki, Georgia

Senaki grew into an important western Georgian town after the 1871 Poti-Tbilisi railway spurred development; it was renamed Tskhakaia in 1933 in honor of a Soviet revolutionary before reverting to Senaki in 1989. A small trading Jewish community formed in the early 20th century, growing from 40 residents in 1910 to about 400 by 1939 and 741 by 1976, drawing migrants from Bandza, Kulashi, Vani, and Sujuna; by the 1970s, Senaki had become a significant center of Jewish life in western Georgia. A stone synagogue was built in 1880. Tombstones in this cemetery were mostly placed in the second half of the 20th century, with use continuing through 2003; some illegible stones may date earlier.
